CVE-2026-103582.title: Apache ActiveMQ NMS OpenWire Client Library: Unbounded/Unvalidated Length Fields in Apache.NMS.OpenWire Unmarshalling (DoS)
CVE-2026-103582.description:
Unbounded memory allocation and missing frame size validation in Apache NMS ActiveMQ (the .NET OpenWire client, package Apache.NMS.ActiveMQ) before 2.3.0.

The OpenWire unmarshalling code trusted the frame size and the length and count fields read from the network. It did not enforce a maximum frame size, and it did not check that decoded lengths fit within the frame being read. A malicious or compromised broker, or an attacker able to intercept and modify an unencrypted connection, could send a crafted OpenWire frame with an oversized or negative length. This could cause the client to attempt very large memory allocations, leading to excessive memory consumption, an OutOfMemoryException or an uncaught exception, and a denial of service of the client application.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.3.0, which enforces a configurable maximum frame size and validates lengths against the size of the frame being read.

affected.product: Apache ActiveMQ NMS OpenWire Client Library

CVE-2026-115866.title: Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regular expression backtracking when decoding chunked request bodies
CVE-2026-115866.description:
Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regular expression backtracking when decoding chunked request bodies.

A chunk-size line is matched as a run of hex digits, then .* and a CRLF. A run followed by a bare LF and then a CRLF can never match, and the engine retries the match once for each digit, so the time taken grows with the square of the run length. Nothing limits the length of the run, which can span several reads.

A remote attacker can occupy a worker for about a minute of CPU time with one 128 KiB request, before the application is called.

CVE-2026-133750.title: CachingHttpClient Shares Responses Between Users When Credentials Are Set With withOptions()
CVE-2026-133750.description:
Since Symfony 7.4, CachingHttpClient can cache the responses of HTTP clients, for example when caching is enabled in framework.http_client. Its withOptions() method passes the options to the decorated client only. So credentials set with withOptions(), like auth_bearer, auth_basic, an Authorization header or a Cookie header, reach the server, but CachingHttpClient doesn't see them. They're missing from the cache key. They also miss the rule that keeps a shared cache from storing the responses to requests with an Authorization header. A cacheable response fetched for one user is then served to the next users:

$client->withOptions(['auth_bearer' => $aliceToken])->request('GET', 'https://api.example.com/me'); // Alice's profile
$client->withOptions(['auth_bearer' => $bobToken])->request('GET', 'https://api.example.com/me'); // Alice's profile, from the cache

Applications are affected when they enable caching on a client, set per-user credentials with withOptions(), and request URLs…

CVE-2026-99412.title: xfs: avoid cross-rtgroup reaping after a repair
CVE-2026-99412.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: avoid cross-rtgroup reaping after a repair

LOLLM notices that the extents stored in a xrtb_bitmap (aka xfs_rtblock
bitmap) can span multiple rtgroups due to two circumstances. The first
is that the size of an rtgroup is an exact power of two, which means
that rtgroups are adjacent in the segmented xfs_rtblock_t address space.
This is fairly common to reduce the amount of multiplication and
division needed to handle space on the rt volume.

The second is that (unlike in the original rtgroups design), rtgroups do
not have fixed-location metadata like AGs do, which means that there's
nothing to force a break between rtgroups.

Therefore, we must loop through the rtgroups in xreap_rtmeta_extent to
avoid running off the end of an rtgroup while reaping.

CVE-2026-99661.title: mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast
CVE-2026-99661.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast

The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to
start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated
the length on 32bit.

Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts
from a 64-bit userspace length.

Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with
-EOVERFLOW early.
